1.2 The registered office of the Initiative shall be situated at No. 14 Dan Agundi Road, Kano Municipal, Kano State, Nigeria. The Board of Trustees may, by resolution, change the registered office address, provided that notice of such change is duly filed with the Corporate Affairs Commission.

ARTICLE 2: AIMS AND OBJECTIVES

2.1 The principal aims and objectives of the Initiative shall be:

(a) To improve access to quality primary healthcare services for underserved communities in Kano State and its environs;

(b) To design, implement, and evaluate community-based health education programs addressing maternal and child health, infectious disease prevention, and hygiene promotion;

(c) To organize and conduct immunization outreach activities in collaboration with state and local government health authorities;

(d) To build the capacity of community health workers through training and mentorship;

(e) To advocate for equitable health policies and resource allocation that benefit vulnerable populations;

(f) To establish partnerships with governmental, non-governmental, and international agencies in furtherance of the above objectives; and

(g) To engage in any other lawful activity incidental or conducive to the attainment of the foregoing objectives.

ARTICLE 3: BOARD OF TRUSTEES

3.1 The affairs of the Initiative shall be managed by a Board of Trustees comprising not less than five (5) and not more than nine (9) members.

3.2 The inaugural Board of Trustees shall consist of the persons named in the Schedule hereto.

3.3 Trustees shall hold office for a term of three (3) years, renewable subject to satisfactory performance and re-appointment by the Board.

3.4 A Trustee may be removed from office by a resolution passed by a two-thirds majority of the remaining Trustees at a meeting duly convened for that purpose, on grounds of incapacity, misconduct, or conduct prejudicial to the interests of the Initiative.

ARTICLE 4: MEETINGS

4.1 The Board of Trustees shall meet at least once every quarter. The Chairman may convene an emergency meeting upon the written request of at least two Trustees.

The Kano Community Health Initiative (KCHI) was founded on 2019-03-14. Record status: current.

4.2 Notice of any meeting shall be given in writing to each Trustee at least seven (7) days prior to the date of the meeting, except in the case of an emergency meeting, where notice of at least forty-eight (48) hours shall be given.

4.3 The quorum for a meeting of the Board of Trustees shall be one-half of the total number of Trustees.

4.4 Each Trustee shall have one vote. In the case of an equality of votes, the Chairman of the meeting shall have a second or casting vote.

ARTICLE 5: OFFICERS

5.1 The officers of the Initiative shall be:

(a) Chairman
(b) Vice-Chairman
(c) Secretary
(d) Treasurer

5.2 Officers shall be elected by the Board of Trustees from among its members at the first meeting following the adoption of this Constitution.

5.3 The Secretary shall be responsible for keeping the minutes of all meetings, maintaining the official records of the Initiative, and conducting correspondence on behalf of the Board.

5.4 The Treasurer shall be responsible for the custody of funds, maintenance of financial records, and the preparation of annual accounts for submission to the Board and, where required, to relevant authorities.

ARTICLE 6: FINANCE AND ACCOUNTING

6.1 The funds of the Initiative shall be derived from grants, donations, subscriptions, and such other lawful sources as the Board may determine.

6.2 All funds shall be kept in a bank account or accounts in the name of the Initiative, and withdrawals shall require the signatures of at least two authorized signatories, one of whom shall be the Treasurer or Chairman.

6.3 The financial year of the Initiative shall run from 1 January to 31 December of each year.

6.4 The accounts of the Initiative shall be audited annually by an independent auditor appointed by the Board.

ARTICLE 7: AMENDMENT OF CONSTITUTION

7.1 This Constitution may be amended by a resolution passed by a two-thirds majority of the Board of Trustees at a meeting duly convened for that purpose, provided that such amendment is consistent with the regulations of the Corporate Affairs Commission.

ARTICLE 4: MEETINGS OF THE BOARD

4.1 The Board shall hold an Annual General Meeting within six (6) months of the end of each financial year. Notice of every Annual General Meeting shall be given in writing to each Trustee not less than twenty-one (21) days before the date of the meeting.

4.2 The quorum for a meeting of the Board shall be one-half of the total number of Trustees, or three (3) Trustees, whichever is greater. No business shall be transacted at any meeting unless the quorum is present at the commencement of the meeting.

4.3 The Chairman shall preside at all meetings of the Board. In the absence of the Chairman, the Vice Chairman shall preside. In the absence of both, the Trustees present shall elect one of their number to chair the meeting.

4.4 Minutes of every meeting shall be recorded and kept by the Secretary in a minute book provided for that purpose. The minutes shall be confirmed at the next meeting and signed by the Chairman.

4.5 Decisions of the Board shall be by simple majority of the Trustees present and voting. In the case of an equality of votes, the Chairman shall have a second or casting vote.

ARTICLE 5: OFFICERS OF THE ORGANIZATION

5.1 The Organization may appoint such officers and staff as the Board may from time to time consider necessary for the efficient management of its affairs. The principal officers shall include the Executive Director, the Program Manager, the Finance Officer, and such other officers as the Board may determine.

5.2 The Executive Director shall be the chief executive officer of the Organization and shall be responsible for the day-to-day administration of the Organization, subject to the general direction and control of the Board.

5.3 The Finance Officer shall be responsible for the preparation of budgets, the keeping of proper books of account, and the preparation of financial statements for submission to the Board and to external auditors.

ARTICLE 6: FINANCE AND ACCOUNTING

6.1 The financial year of the Organization shall begin on the 1st day of January and end on the 31st day of December of each year.

6.2 The Board shall cause proper books of account to be kept with respect to:
a) All sums of money received and expended by the Organization and the matters in respect of which such receipts and expenditure take place;
b) All sales and purchases of goods and services by the Organization; and
c) The assets and liabilities of the Organization.

6.3 The books of account shall be kept at the head office of the Organization, or at such other place as the Board may think fit, and shall always be open to inspection by any Trustee.

6.6 The Organization may pay reasonable honoraria to volunteers and community health committee members for services rendered, provided that such payments are approved by the Board and recorded in the minutes.

ARTICLE 7: COMMUNITY HEALTH COMMITTEES

7.1 The Organization may establish community health committees in the communities where it operates. Each committee shall consist of not fewer than five (5) and not more than eleven (11) members, appointed by the Board upon recommendation of the Executive Director.

7.2 The functions of a community health committee shall include:
a) Mobilizing community members for health education sessions, immunization drives, and screening camps;
b) Identifying local health priorities and communicating them to the Organization;
c) Assisting in the distribution of health-related materials and commodities;
d) Providing feedback on the effectiveness of the Organization's programs.
